doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Ernie Watts
summary: Lamb praises Ernie Watts, and Rowe relays Watts' story of learning on hard music like Giant Steps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah I interviewed him years ago.

Do you know how he is? Have you had any contact with him? Because I haven’t for years. He lived over near Aspen, he lived in Carbondale, so he was another guy I could reach out to and grab and pull in. He was, what an incredible musician that dude is. What a vocabulary he had and just a sweetheart of a guy you know, just embracing of everybody. Great charts.

He said something interesting, that he learned — the first music he learned was very difficult music — like “Giant Steps” and he didn’t know it was hard. So anything that came after that, like all that studio work he did and laying in solos on all those records was — I’m not sure what adjective he used but he had learned on the hardest stuff there was.
That’s great. What a neat thing man, because everything is easier after that, you know if you tackle that out of the gate.
Well you could almost say the same thing, you heard Chick Corea and Return to Forever when you were just in your yout’.
